| Human operational records | `operational_record` has stable record ID, typed kind (such as fuel delivery), author, occurrence interval, recorded time, unit/quantity, source document hash and correction chain. It is separate from `accepted_evidence`, which remains device/gateway sourced. | Attested content is immutable; correction points to superseded record and reason. Reconciliation is a revisioned analytic result over chosen record/evidence IDs. | Fuel balance, service request and backup test calculations cite both operational-record IDs and accepted source evidence IDs with distinct provenance labels. | Policies and tenant settings | `policy` has stable key and explicit scope (`tenant`, `site`, or domain); `policy_revision` carries valid/recorded time, author and immutable content. Existing `tenant` remains estate identity; `tenant_configuration_revision` owns editable settings once auth exists. | Publishing locks the scope and forbids overlapping current validity per key; corrections append and preserve prior knowledge. Role/permission changes have separate audit events. | Analytic/verification inputs retain exact policy revision IDs. A policy is declared authority, not proof of controller application; applied change has its own artifact/event. | Define policy vocabulary, who may publish, scope precedence, authentication/roles and audit before Settings is writable. |
| Financial scenarios | `financial_scenario` has stable Site/tenant-scoped scenario identity and owner; `financial_scenario_revision` freezes assumption revision IDs, window, parameters and formula version. | A new edit creates a revision; scenario runs/results are append-only, keyed by scenario revision and input digest. | Scenario consequence cites source Finding/quantity revision where used, and is always labelled `Scenario`. It cannot overwrite a measured/modelled operational consequence or be counted as recovered money. | Define allowed variables, cross-site scope, comparison baseline and currency/period rules before the Scenarios tab is live. |
| Site onboarding | `site_draft` has its own UUID and tenant-scoped proposed code, separate from published `site.id`. `site_template` reuses the shipped catalog only as an explicitly versioned input; `site_import_batch` has stable upload identity and per-row disposition. | Draft revisions and setup events are append-only. Publish atomically allocates/resolves the Site code, initial Foundation and source registration; a failed batch row leaves no partial Site. Template updates never rewrite published Sites. | Persist source digest/template version and actor for every published Site; link import-row receipt to resulting Site/Foundation IDs. Imported physical/evidence claims still need gateway registration and accepted envelopes. | Define draft expiration, duplicate-code arbitration, template migration, batch atomicity/per-row retry and tenant authorization. **Shared projection rule.** `CapabilityReadiness`, `FindingIndex`, `SourceHealth`, `AssetHealthSummary` and later `MaintenanceIndex` have multiple screen consumers. Their first implementation must publish a backend read-model contract with scope/window, stable sort/pagination, freshness watermark, revision and drill-down IDs, Unknown/NotApplicable semantics and tenant isolation. A Site projection can feed a global root only after aggregation semantics are declared; shared names in the mock do not imply that the first Site query already serves the estate. `MaintenanceIndex` waits on maintenance identities above.

**Root ownership rule before S4 and S6.** The Site Findings list is a Site-scoped projection; a Finding detail, Analysis, Evidence, Alternatives, Recommendation and History share stable Finding identity in the Findings root. S4's first detail route must preserve that identity and selected revision across tabs and links back to the Site. The Site Work list is a Site-scoped projection; Action Overview, Plan, Execution, Evidence, Verification and History share stable Action identity in the Actions root. Before S6 verification, define the Action-root route and plan/outcome revision URLs, preserving the Site/Finding back-links. Unimplemented tabs stay hidden; an empty tab must represent a real supported question.

**Demo data dependency.** One Kobo window cannot substantiate the multi-site, multi-window, cold-chain or EV mock claims. Before their packets, define a small seed manifest per Site/window with source mode, Foundation/binding versions, gateway fixture, accepted/rejected evidence, analytic version, assumptions and expected claim limits. Rehearse both a complete and an Unknown/contradictory case through normal ingestion; do not stage Findings or prices directly. Portfolio requires comparable periods, currency, coverage and overlap rules across the seeded Sites.
# Site-first execution plan

**Planner handoff Â· 2026-10-06.** The accepted [system architecture](production-shaped-mvp.md) and [platform technical design](production-shaped-mvp-technical-design.md) are frozen inputs. This plan sequences implementation; it does not amend those decisions or revive the old T0xx queue. The seven rows are **product milestones**, each possibly split by the Planner into a few small tasks. A milestone closes only when its named Site mock surface shows real persisted data and the cited evidence can be opened.

```text
  â†’ Site Health

simulated or physical report â†’ edge SQLite â†’ SourceEnvelope â†’ shared ingestion

```

Start with **one mini-grid Site and one assessed window**. Use the existing causal simulator as the S2â€“S7 producer. A physical protocol capture or labelled vendor-format fixture becomes a contract peer at the first real pilot, once an input is available. Retain the static v6.9 mock screens as interaction/content references; a slice implements the supported portion with honest missing states, not a full static screen filled with invented data. Existing JSON/YAML data stays available for migration comparison, but new product writes use the target stores. The Site shell can keep its current routes and reusable components where they help.

S2 is intentionally a large **milestone**: split gateway acquisition, Postgres acceptance and Evidence UI into reviewable tasks under one acceptance checkpoint if necessary. ## Planner instruction: replace the task queue

The accepted architecture and this Site-first sequence supersede the **open** T0xx implementation queue. Make this change explicit before writing new task packets:

The recorded diagnostics contract is a separate authenticated `GatewayDiagnosticsV1` report rather than a `SourceEnvelope`: registered gateway/site identity, observation time, local sequence, last device contact by source, queue count and oldest age, disk pressure, clock offset and mapping errors. The server records its own receipt time and computes central freshness from that time and a declared cadence; a missing heartbeat is Unknown/stale, never a healthy reading. Reports are idempotent by gateway/sequence and are not accepted telemetry. The [technical design](production-shaped-mvp-technical-design.md) now owns the table, endpoint and wire fields; S2-01c/S2-02 packets refine cadence and focused crash tests.

**Physical peer source in effect:** S2 uses simulated reports only. That future gate replaces the simulator batch while preserving the backend, analytic and UI contracts. It is not an S2 acceptance check. The S7 demo cannot use captured-device replay as a battery fallback under this source choice.

## Shared implementation rules

- **Immediate demo scope versus target design:** S1â€“S2 need crash-safe SQLite enqueue, stable identities, authenticated batch ingestion, durable per-record decisions and Postgres Site/evidence storage. Build the minimal diagnostics needed to inspect delivery. Detailed queue retention policy, elaborate backpressure controls, multi-protocol drivers, broker transport, full bitemporal editing UI and generic streaming infrastructure can follow when pilots require them. Database/wire schemas should leave room without falsely claiming those behaviors are shipped.
- **Typed analytic boundary:** `EvidenceQuery` returns typed normalized readings/records with quality, time, asset/role, configuration basis and accepted-evidence IDs. The dispatch analytic consumes this plus a typed public configuration view. SQL rows, `jsonb`, canonical envelope text, Lab world records and source adapters stop at repository/normalization boundaries. Contract tests compare simulated and captured real inputs after this boundary.
- **Episode identity:** decide continuity tolerance, episode anchor and recurrence linkage in S3/S4 domain design, with a short decision table before coding the first Finding. `Finding.id` names a durable operational episode; `FindingRevision` describes reassessment of that episode. A new separated episode is a new Finding, linked as recurrence if relevant. Do not use a changing model output hash as Finding identity.
- **Domain algorithms:** dispatch thresholds, cold-chain excursion detection and EV session logic are domain-design work. The platform plan requires their inputs, revision/lineage outputs and claim limits, not more universal framework or algorithm prose. S1â€“S7 cover one mini-grid Site; later domains add role sets and analytics through the same seam.
- **Verification gates:** each slice exercises the screen at its selected window, the read API, storage/reload, a missing/contradictory evidence case, and lineage back to an accepted SourceEnvelope. S2 adds loss/retry/duplicate/conflict; S3â€“S4 add late evidence and revision preservation; S6 adds guardrail failure. Tests should assert behavior, not mock labels.

## Handoff beyond Site

After S4, a **Findings index** can already list real Finding objects, but build the global root only when the Site detail and lifecycle are useful. After S6, **Actions** and **Sites** become filtering/indexing over durable Site/Action summaries; **Portfolio** aggregates comparable consequences and priorities with currency/window/coverage boundaries; **Evidence** aggregates Site capability/readiness; **Assets** indexes Site Asset/Health/work records after S7. These are later product roots, not prerequisites or empty screens for the Site spine. Cold-chain and EV are later Site-domain passes using the same ingestion, revision, work and shell contracts; neither should be built by copying mini-grid screens with different labels.

## Outcome and authority

An accepted late generator-power mean that can alter an existing Site FindingRevision's `fuel-cost-1` input creates durable consequence work in the same database transaction as acceptance. The Site read shows the old consequence as `STALE` (or `PENDING` if no consequence exists) with real queued work, then a scheduled, retryable worker derives and appends the new exact-basis consequence. The S5-01 selected-window read may use money only after that consequence is `CURRENT` and `PRICED` for its selected FindingRevision and window. A fresh stale read alone does not complete this slice.

## Acceptance, work and worker contract

1. Add a migration to extend `financial_consequence_work` with an `EVIDENCE_ACCEPTED` cause and a tenant/Site-scoped FK to the exact `accepted_evidence.id`. Keep existing assumption and FindingRevision causes and rows valid. Each new row identifies the accepted evidence, target Finding and latest eligible FindingRevision at enqueue time, and its half-open affected interval. Constrain cause shape, range, scope and a unique `(accepted_evidence_id, finding_revision_id, cause)` key; duplicates and conflicting evidence create no second row. Index pending selection by Site and due time. Preserve append-only evidence, work and attempt history. Migration upgrade/downgrade and pre-existing rows must be proved.
2. In the S2-02 acceptance transaction, after a genuinely new accepted evidence ID is returned, select potentially affected existing Site Findings by coarse half-open interval overlap with the accepted interval and the **server-bound** `generator_power` role (`fuel_cost.POWER_ROLE`). Insert scoped work before commit. If the insert fails, acceptance and its disposition roll back; it must never leave a committed accepted reading with a lost required work row. Exact replay, duplicate, conflict and rejected decisions do not enqueue. If the transaction contains several accepted intervals, each exact accepted ID is deduplicated against its target. Do not trigger on a client-declared role or from a later read. Broad selection may queue a candidate that later no-ops, but must not omit a possibly affected Finding. FindingRevision insertion retains migration 0011's own trigger so findings first created after acceptance also get work.
3. The worker treats the queued revision as a locator, then rechecks tenant/Site, accepted disposition, bound role/asset, half-open interval overlap, candidate episode/window and the **latest eligible FindingRevision** for that Finding at processing time. Derive against that exact current revision and its accepted public inputs only. A superseded or irrelevant target records a successful typed no-op; if a newer eligible revision exists, process that revision once (its insertion trigger may also queue it). No-op on unrelated roles/assets/windows without appending a consequence. A missing or closed source stays typed and retryable when transient; wrong-Site scope never falls back. Price and technical basis selection remain the reviewed S4-02b contract; no extra amount or quantity shortcut is introduced. The existing unique consequence basis and append lock must make unchanged or repeated work return the existing ID, including concurrent workers and an append-then-crash retry.
4. Make the run plan operational: extend the server-side CLI to drain a configured tenant/Site (or a scoped active-Site iterator) on a documented one-minute recurring service/timer, with bounded batch size, a database claim/lease or equivalent single-consumer lock, persisted retry eligibility/backoff, and a restart-safe failure record. A failed item remains visible but cannot hot-loop inside one run; a later scheduled run retries it. Print/record selected, appended, replayed, no-op, failed and backlog counts with Site scope; document deployment invocation, ownership, cadence and recovery. The scheduler must not rely on a user opening Financials. Existing price/Finding work uses the same runner. A work item becomes succeeded only after all its selected targets have safely appended/replayed or no-opped; crash and concurrent-run tests must prove eventual drain without duplicate consequence basis.
5. Keep the consequence read's `CURRENT`/`STALE`/`PENDING`/`HISTORICAL` and typed reasons. Show queued/pending status only when a real unsucceeded work row touches the selected revision; if currentness is stale but no work exists, report that discrepancy explicitly and do not claim queued. S5-01 uses only a `CURRENT`/`PRICED`, same Site/window/FindingRevision/basis consequence after work finishes. No new UI copy or mock panel is authorized here; a necessary owner-facing copy change reopens `USER_REVIEW_REQUIRED` and its checkpoint.

### L3 (Low): unknown causes fall through in the existing worker

`ConsequenceRecomputeWorker.targets()` treats any non-`FINDING_REVISION_APPENDED` cause as an assumption range. If phase 1 is merged or run before phase 2, an `EVIDENCE_ACCEPTED` row is drained as a Site-wide overlap recompute and marked SUCCEEDED, which loses its typed recheck. Phase 1 should make an unknown cause a typed FAILED attempt (or skip it), or the packet should state that phases 1-3 merge together.

0011 bootstrapped pre-existing FindingRevisions (review L4). Here, late power accepted before 0012 leaves `STALE` heads with no work forever. Phase 1 (migration, trigger and tests) and phase 3 (walkthrough) each fit one context. Phase 2 is the heaviest: worker recheck, no-op, claim and backoff, the CLI loop, runner documentation, and M2's read change if placed there. It probably still fits under ~120k, provided the claim mechanism is pinned (M1). Otherwise, move the read change (M2) to phase 1. Each phase's proofs are non-vacuous once H1, H2 and M4 are added.

## Carries for the Implementer (after the Planner amendment)

- C1: Prove H2 explicitly. Insert a FindingRevision after 0012 and assert one `FINDING_REVISION_APPENDED` row. Insert an `EVIDENCE_ACCEPTED` row for the same revision and assert both coexist. Run the 0011 bootstrap rows through upgrade, then downgrade per M5.
- C2: Rule 8 must still pass unchanged (or with the named amendment). Assert in a test that no Python module inserts into `financial_consequence_work`.
- C3: Half-open edge tests at both ends: a reading ending exactly at `episode_start` and one starting exactly at `episode_end` do not enqueue. A zero-width episode never enqueues.
- C4: Foreign-Site proof: an accepted reading at Site B with identical times enqueues nothing for Site A, and the worker refuses a forged cross-Site locator with no fallback.
- C5: Record exact work, attempt and consequence IDs, and the `examined_evidence_ids` before and after, in the walkthrough artifact. Record no mock money.

## Residual risks the packet does not name

- **R1:** After late evidence, S5 current money depends on S3 `process-jobs` and S4 `match-findings`, which are still one-shot and unscheduled. S4-02c schedules only the consequence drain. `D-2026-10-14-s5-selected-window-overview` already makes S5 show `PENDING`/`STALE` while analytic work is dirty, so this is honest. In practice, though, a late reading leaves Overview money unavailable until someone runs those CLIs. This is optional for the Architect: does S3/S4 runner scheduling become its own follow-on before W1 exit, or does S4-02c's runner also drive them? It is not a blocker for this packet.
- **R2:** Row volume. There is one work row per (accepted generator-power evidence x overlapping Finding). A gateway backfill of a day of 5-minute means across many Findings creates hundreds of rows per Site. This is acceptable at the current scale, but bounded batch size (item 4) should be tested against such a backfill.

"""S4-02b phase 1: append-only financial consequence revisions, lineage links and durable dirty work.

`D-2026-10-13-s4-bounded-financial-basis` (and its `fuel-cost-1` addendum); packet
`tasks/S4-02b-fuel-consequence.md` "Migration, recompute and reads". This supersedes the technical design's
single-assessment / single-assumption / scalar-quantity sketch (review carry L1): rows carry explicit
`quantity_low/high`, a separate technical-input digest and consequence basis digest, and multi-row links.

- `financial_consequence_revision`: one immutable `POTENTIAL_FUEL_COST` consequence of one exact
  FindingRevision, `MODELLED_CONDITIONAL`, with the `fuel-cost-1` parameter version, quantity bounds, the
  whole-window price selection and nullable amount bounds. CHECKs make an unavailable quantity carry no
  number, an unpriced consequence carry no amount and a priced one carry exactly `0 .. quantity_high x price`.
  UNIQUE `(finding_revision_id, consequence_type, revision_no)` and `(finding_revision_id, consequence_type,
  consequence_basis_sha256)` (idempotent append).
- Links: `financial_consequence_assessment_revision` (primary plus every supporting exact assessment, each
  required to be linked by the FindingRevision itself), `financial_consequence_assumption_revision` (every
  exact price revision used) and `financial_consequence_power_interval` (each counted accepted power mean once,
  with power, duration, SFC revision, covered Candidate spans and containment result).
- Dirty/outbox: `financial_consequence_work` rows are inserted only by triggers, in the same transaction as an
  assumption publication or a FindingRevision append, keyed by Site, key/revision or FindingRevision and the
  affected valid range. `financial_consequence_work_attempt` records each recompute attempt (phase 2a worker);
  work without a SUCCEEDED attempt is pending. FindingRevisions that predate this migration are enqueued once
  by the upgrade itself (review L4), so no Finding is left with neither a consequence nor pending work.

Revises: 0010_financial_assumptions
Create Date: 2026-10-14

-- A consequence names its own FindingRevision's Finding and window, and extends its chain by exactly one.
CREATE FUNCTION financial_consequence_revision_lineage() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
DECLARE
    fr finding_revision%ROWTYPE;
    prior financial_consequence_revision%ROWTYPE;
    latest integer;
BEGIN
    SELECT * INTO fr FROM finding_revision
        WHERE tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND site_id = NEW.site_id AND id = NEW.finding_revision_id;
    IF fr.finding_id IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.finding_id THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'financial_consequence_revision names a FindingRevision of another Finding';
    END IF;
    IF fr.episode_start IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.window_start OR fr.episode_end IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.window_end THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'financial_consequence_revision window is not its FindingRevision window';
    END IF;
    -- Review L6: a priced row's value and currency are its price revision's own.
    IF NEW.price_revision_id IS NOT NULL AND NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM financial_assumption_revision p WHERE p.tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND p.site_id = NEW.site_id
          AND p.id = NEW.price_revision_id AND p.assumption_key = 'diesel_price_per_litre'
          AND p.value = NEW.price_value AND p.currency = NEW.price_currency) THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'financial_consequence_revision price is not its price revision''s value and currency';
    END IF;
    SELECT max(revision_no) INTO latest FROM financial_consequence_revision
        WHERE finding_revision_id = NEW.finding_revision_id AND consequence_type = NEW.consequence_type;
    IF NEW.revision_no <> coalesce(latest, 0) + 1 THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'financial_consequence_revision revision_no must extend its chain by one';
    END IF;
    IF NEW.prior_consequence_revision_id IS NOT NULL THEN
        SELECT * INTO prior FROM financial_consequence_revision WHERE id = NEW.prior_consequence_revision_id;
        IF prior.finding_revision_id IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.finding_revision_id
           OR prior.consequence_type IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.consequence_type
           OR prior.revision_no IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.revision_no - 1 THEN
            RAISE EXCEPTION 'financial_consequence_revision prior is not the previous revision of its chain';
        END IF;
    END IF;
    RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;
CREATE TRIGGER financial_consequence_revision_lineage BEFORE INSERT ON financial_consequence_revision
    FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION financial_consequence_revision_lineage();

-- Review L6, at commit: a priced row has its PRICE link, and the assessment links are exactly the
-- FindingRevision's INTERVAL assessments.
CREATE FUNCTION financial_consequence_links_complete() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN
    IF NEW.state = 'PRICED' AND NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM financial_consequence_assumption_revision l WHERE l.consequence_revision_id = NEW.id
          AND l.assumption_revision_id = NEW.price_revision_id AND l.role = 'PRICE') THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'financial_consequence_revision is PRICED without its PRICE link';
    END IF;
    IF EXISTS (
        (SELECT a.assessment_revision_id, a.analytic_run_id, a.is_primary FROM finding_revision_assessment a
          WHERE a.finding_revision_id = NEW.finding_revision_id AND a.scope = 'INTERVAL'
         EXCEPT SELECT l.assessment_revision_id, l.analytic_run_id, l.is_primary
          FROM financial_consequence_assessment_revision l WHERE l.consequence_revision_id = NEW.id)) THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'financial_consequence_revision does not link every INTERVAL assessment of its FindingRevision';
    END IF;
    RETURN NULL;
END;
$$;
CREATE CONSTRAINT TRIGGER financial_consequence_links_complete AFTER INSERT ON financial_consequence_revision
    DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION financial_consequence_links_complete();

-- A consequence may cite only assessments its FindingRevision itself links.
CREATE FUNCTION financial_consequence_assessment_linked() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN
    IF NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM financial_consequence_revision c
        JOIN finding_revision_assessment a ON a.finding_revision_id = c.finding_revision_id
        WHERE c.id = NEW.consequence_revision_id AND a.assessment_revision_id = NEW.assessment_revision_id
          AND a.analytic_run_id = NEW.analytic_run_id AND a.scope = 'INTERVAL' AND a.is_primary = NEW.is_primary) THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'financial_consequence_assessment_revision is not an INTERVAL assessment of its FindingRevision';
    END IF;
    RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;
CREATE TRIGGER financial_consequence_assessment_linked BEFORE INSERT ON financial_consequence_assessment_revision
    FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION financial_consequence_assessment_linked();

-- Transactional dirty work: an assumption publication dirties its affected valid range (a SUCCESSION also
-- changes everything after its start, because it closes the prior open-ended assignment there).
CREATE FUNCTION financial_consequence_dirty_on_assumption() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN
    INSERT INTO financial_consequence_work (tenant_id, site_id, cause, assumption_key, assumption_revision_id,
                                            affected_from, affected_to)
    VALUES (NEW.tenant_id, NEW.site_id, 'ASSUMPTION_PUBLISHED', NEW.assumption_key, NEW.id, NEW.valid_from,
            CASE WHEN NEW.change_kind = 'SUCCESSION' THEN NULL ELSE NEW.valid_to END)
    ON CONFLICT (assumption_revision_id) DO NOTHING;
    RETURN NULL;
END;
$$;
CREATE TRIGGER financial_consequence_dirty_on_assumption AFTER INSERT ON financial_assumption_revision
    FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION financial_consequence_dirty_on_assumption();

CREATE FUNCTION financial_consequence_dirty_on_finding_revision() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN
    INSERT INTO financial_consequence_work (tenant_id, site_id, cause, finding_id, finding_revision_id,
                                            affected_from, affected_to)
    VALUES (NEW.tenant_id, NEW.site_id, 'FINDING_REVISION_APPENDED', NEW.finding_id, NEW.id, NEW.episode_start,
            NEW.episode_end)
    ON CONFLICT (finding_revision_id) DO NOTHING;
    RETURN NULL;
END;
$$;
CREATE TRIGGER financial_consequence_dirty_on_finding_revision AFTER INSERT ON finding_revision
    FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION financial_consequence_dirty_on_finding_revision();

-- Review L4 (bootstrap): FindingRevisions recorded before this migration get the same work row the trigger
-- would have written, so the recompute worker derives their consequences with the current price.
INSERT INTO financial_consequence_work (tenant_id, site_id, cause, finding_id, finding_revision_id, affected_from,
                                        affected_to)
SELECT tenant_id, site_id, 'FINDING_REVISION_APPENDED', finding_id, id, episode_start, episode_end
FROM finding_revision ORDER BY created_at, id;
"""

"""Durable `fuel-cost-1` consequence recompute (S4-02b phase 2a).

Packet `tasks/S4-02b-fuel-consequence.md` "Migration, recompute and reads": dirty work rows are written by
migration 0011's triggers in the assumption-publication or FindingRevision transaction (and once for every
FindingRevision that predates 0011). This worker drains them:

    pending_work -> load_input -> quantify -> select_window_price -> consequence -> append -> record_attempt

- `FINDING_REVISION_APPENDED` recomputes that exact FindingRevision (a new FindingRevision gets its own
  consequence chain, even when a later revision has since superseded it).
- `ASSUMPTION_PUBLISHED` recomputes the latest revision of every Finding whose episode overlaps the
  publication's affected valid range `[affected_from, affected_to)`.

Each target is derived from the exact persisted inputs and the price timeline known now, and appended
idempotently: an unchanged basis replays the stored ID (review M1 keeps an unrelated publication from
re-revising), a changed one appends revision n+1. A failure records a typed FAILED attempt and leaves the work
pending, so the read shows STALE/PENDING rather than an old amount as current; the next run retries. A crash
between `append` and `record_attempt` is safe: the retry replays the same consequence ID.

This module does no I/O of its own; stores are injected (composition builds them).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any, Protocol
from uuid import UUID

from assetops_backend.financials import fuel_cost as fc

ERROR_STORE_UNAVAILABLE = "STORE_UNAVAILABLE"
ERROR_FINDING_REVISION_NOT_FOUND = "FINDING_REVISION_NOT_FOUND"
ERROR_RECOMPUTE_FAILED = "RECOMPUTE_FAILED"


class ConsequenceStore(Protocol):
    def load_input(self, tenant_id: UUID, site_id: UUID, finding_id: UUID,
                   finding_revision_id: UUID) -> fc.FindingInput | None: ...

    def append(self, c_: fc.Consequence) -> Any: ...

    def pending_work(self, tenant_id: UUID, site_id: UUID) -> list[dict[str, Any]]: ...

    def record_attempt(self, tenant_id: UUID, site_id: UUID, work_id: UUID, **kw: Any) -> int: ...

    def latest_revisions_overlapping(self, tenant_id: UUID, site_id: UUID, lo: Any,
                                     hi: Any) -> list[tuple[UUID, UUID]]: ...


class PriceStore(Protocol):
    def snapshot(self, tenant_id: UUID, site_id: UUID, key: str, recorded_at: Any, after_revision_no: int,
                 limit: int) -> dict[str, Any]: ...


class FindingRevisionMissing(LookupError):
    pass


def window_price(prices: PriceStore, tenant_id: UUID, site_id: UUID, f: fc.FindingInput) -> fc.PriceSelection:
    """The whole-window price selection from the current price timeline (recorded cutoff: now)."""
    snap = prices.snapshot(tenant_id, site_id, fc.PRICE_KEY, None, 0, 1)
    return fc.select_window_price(snap["timeline"], snap["cited"], f.window_start, f.window_end)


def derive(store: ConsequenceStore, prices: PriceStore, tenant_id: UUID, site_id: UUID, finding_id: UUID,            return [(work["finding_id"], work["finding_revision_id"])]
        return self._store.latest_revisions_overlapping(tenant_id, site_id, work["affected_from"],
                                                        work["affected_to"])

    def process(self, tenant_id: UUID, site_id: UUID, work: dict[str, Any]) -> WorkOutcome:
        out = WorkOutcome(work["id"], work["cause"], False, 0)
        try:
            for finding_id, revision_id in self.targets(tenant_id, site_id, work):
                appended = self._store.append(derive(self._store, self._prices, tenant_id, site_id, finding_id,
                                                     revision_id))
                out.consequence_revision_ids.append(appended.consequence_revision_id)
                (out.replayed if appended.replayed else out.appended).append(appended.consequence_revision_id)
        except FindingRevisionMissing as error:
            out.error_code, out.error_detail = ERROR_FINDING_REVISION_NOT_FOUND, str(error)
        except self._unavailable as error:
            out.error_code, out.error_detail = ERROR_STORE_UNAVAILABLE, str(error)
        except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - any failure is recorded as typed pending work, never lost
            out.error_code, out.error_detail = ERROR_RECOMPUTE_FAILED, f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}"
        if out.error_code is None:
            out.succeeded = True
            out.attempt_no = self._store.record_attempt(
                tenant_id, site_id, work["id"], succeeded=True,
                consequence_revision_ids=tuple(out.consequence_revision_ids), skip_if_succeeded=True)
        else:
            out.attempt_no = self._store.record_attempt(
                tenant_id, site_id, work["id"], succeeded=False, error_code=out.error_code,
                error_detail=out.error_detail[:2000] if out.error_detail else None)
        return out

    def run_pending(self, tenant_id: UUID, site_id: UUID, limit: int | None = None) -> list[WorkOutcome]:
        """Drain this Site's pending work oldest first; failed items stay pending for the next run."""
        pending = self._store.pending_work(tenant_id, site_id)
        return [self.process(tenant_id, site_id, w) for w in pending[:limit]]

"""Server-side recompute of `fuel-cost-1` consequences (S4-02b phase 2a).        return 2
    url = database_url()
    prices = build_assumption_store(url) if prices is None else prices
    try:
        scope = prices.site_scope(args.tenant, args.site)
        if scope is None:
            print(f"No imported Site {args.site!r} in tenant {args.tenant!r}; nothing was recomputed.",
                  file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
        code, tenant_id, site_id = scope
        if args.command == "pending":
            store = build_consequence_store(url) if store is None else store
            for w in store.pending_work(tenant_id, site_id):
                print(json.dumps({"site_code": code, "work_id": str(w["id"]), "cause": w["cause"],
                                  "attempts": w["attempts"]}))
            return 0
        worker = build_recompute_worker(url) if worker is None else worker
        failed = 0
        for out in worker.run_pending(tenant_id, site_id, args.limit):
            failed += 0 if out.succeeded else 1
            print(json.dumps({"site_code": code, "work_id": str(out.work_id), "cause": out.cause,
                              "succeeded": out.succeeded, "attempt_no": out.attempt_no,

                              "replayed": [str(x) for x in out.replayed],
                              "error_code": out.error_code, "error_detail": out.error_detail}))
        return 1 if failed else 0
    except CONSEQUENCE_UNAVAILABLE as error:
        print(f"The consequence store is unavailable: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 3

 ## Outcome and authority
 
-An accepted late generator-power mean that can alter an existing Site FindingRevision's `fuel-cost-1` input creates durable consequence work in the same database transaction as acceptance. The Site read shows the old consequence as `STALE` (or `PENDING` if no consequence exists) with real queued work, then a scheduled, retryable worker derives and appends the new exact-basis consequence. The S5-01 selected-window read may use money only after that consequence is `CURRENT` and `PRICED` for its selected FindingRevision and window. A fresh stale read alone does not complete this slice.
+A genuinely accepted late generator-power mean that can alter an existing Site FindingRevision's `fuel-cost-1` technical input creates durable consequence work atomically with acceptance. Before drain, the old consequence is `STALE/TECHNICAL_INPUT_CHANGED` (or `PENDING` without a head) with a real queued work ID. Draining that **same** FindingRevision yields a current `QUANTITY_UNAVAILABLE/POWER_NOT_IN_ASSESSMENT_INPUTS` revision: the late reading was not an input to its cited analytic run. S3 `process-jobs` and S4 `match-findings` must re-evaluate the Finding and append a revised FindingRevision before a new `CURRENT/PRICED` consequence can become S5-01 eligible. All revisions remain inspectable. A stale read alone does not complete this slice.

 ## Acceptance, work and worker contract
 
-1. Add a migration to extend `financial_consequence_work` with an `EVIDENCE_ACCEPTED` cause and a tenant/Site-scoped FK to the exact `accepted_evidence.id`. Keep existing assumption and FindingRevision causes and rows valid. Each new row identifies the accepted evidence, target Finding and latest eligible FindingRevision at enqueue time, and its half-open affected interval. Constrain cause shape, range, scope and a unique `(accepted_evidence_id, finding_revision_id, cause)` key; duplicates and conflicting evidence create no second row. Index pending selection by Site and due time. Preserve append-only evidence, work and attempt history. Migration upgrade/downgrade and pre-existing rows must be proved.
-2. In the S2-02 acceptance transaction, after a genuinely new accepted evidence ID is returned, select potentially affected existing Site Findings by coarse half-open interval overlap with the accepted interval and the **server-bound** `generator_power` role (`fuel_cost.POWER_ROLE`). Insert scoped work before commit. If the insert fails, acceptance and its disposition roll back; it must never leave a committed accepted reading with a lost required work row. Exact replay, duplicate, conflict and rejected decisions do not enqueue. If the transaction contains several accepted intervals, each exact accepted ID is deduplicated against its target. Do not trigger on a client-declared role or from a later read. Broad selection may queue a candidate that later no-ops, but must not omit a possibly affected Finding. FindingRevision insertion retains migration 0011's own trigger so findings first created after acceptance also get work.
-3. The worker treats the queued revision as a locator, then rechecks tenant/Site, accepted disposition, bound role/asset, half-open interval overlap, candidate episode/window and the **latest eligible FindingRevision** for that Finding at processing time. Derive against that exact current revision and its accepted public inputs only. A superseded or irrelevant target records a successful typed no-op; if a newer eligible revision exists, process that revision once (its insertion trigger may also queue it). No-op on unrelated roles/assets/windows without appending a consequence. A missing or closed source stays typed and retryable when transient; wrong-Site scope never falls back. Price and technical basis selection remain the reviewed S4-02b contract; no extra amount or quantity shortcut is introduced. The existing unique consequence basis and append lock must make unchanged or repeated work return the existing ID, including concurrent workers and an append-then-crash retry.
-4. Make the run plan operational: extend the server-side CLI to drain a configured tenant/Site (or a scoped active-Site iterator) on a documented one-minute recurring service/timer, with bounded batch size, a database claim/lease or equivalent single-consumer lock, persisted retry eligibility/backoff, and a restart-safe failure record. A failed item remains visible but cannot hot-loop inside one run; a later scheduled run retries it. Print/record selected, appended, replayed, no-op, failed and backlog counts with Site scope; document deployment invocation, ownership, cadence and recovery. The scheduler must not rely on a user opening Financials. Existing price/Finding work uses the same runner. A work item becomes succeeded only after all its selected targets have safely appended/replayed or no-opped; crash and concurrent-run tests must prove eventual drain without duplicate consequence basis.
-5. Keep the consequence read's `CURRENT`/`STALE`/`PENDING`/`HISTORICAL` and typed reasons. Show queued/pending status only when a real unsucceeded work row touches the selected revision; if currentness is stale but no work exists, report that discrepancy explicitly and do not claim queued. S5-01 uses only a `CURRENT`/`PRICED`, same Site/window/FindingRevision/basis consequence after work finishes. No new UI copy or mock panel is authorized here; a necessary owner-facing copy change reopens `USER_REVIEW_REQUIRED` and its checkpoint.

Exact replay, duplicate, conflict and rejected decisions do not enqueue. If the transaction contains several accepted intervals, each exact accepted ID is deduplicated against its target.
